Assign codes only when the decision contains concrete and approved objectives, action plans, actions, commitments, or implementations that are explicitly related to climate adaptation or climate mitigation. Do not classify general policy measures unless their climate relevance is explicit. Use the full surrounding context of the decision to understand the purpose and scope of individual measures. A decision may match multiple codes when supported by its content. When a broader initiative contains sub-goals, measures, or planned work that fall within a taxonomy class, assign the relevant code even when the entire initiative is broader than that class. Be conservative whenever the climate connection or match with a taxonomy class is unclear. Use only codes that occur in the provided code list. Return only a valid JSON list of strings containing the matching codes, or an empty list when no code applies.

Classification rules:
- Classify concrete and approved policy objectives, action plans, actions, commitments, and implementations.
- Assign a code only when the relevant content is explicitly connected to climate adaptation or climate mitigation.
- Do not classify general environmental, spatial, mobility, infrastructure, social, or administrative measures unless their climate relevance is explicit in the decision text.
- Use the full decision and its surrounding context to understand the intent, purpose, and scope of each measure.
- A decision may match multiple taxonomy codes.
- Include a code when a broader initiative contains sub-goals, measures, or planned work that fall within that taxonomy class, even when the broader initiative also covers other subjects.
- Include all codes that are genuinely supported, not merely the most prominent code or a few examples.
- Ignore questions, discussions, exploratory statements, and proposals that have not been concretely approved or committed to.
- Do not infer a climate connection that is not supported by the text.
- Be conservative when the climate relevance or taxonomy match is unclear.
- Use only exact codes appearing in the provided code list.
- Do not invent, alter, explain, or translate codes.
